about.title: About
columns: SAIL (Software & AI Engineering Lab) is a research lab at PUC-Rio dedicated to advancing Software and AI Engineering through rigorous, impactful, and industry-connected research. We investigate how to build, evaluate, and improve software and AI-intensive systems, with interests spanning AI Engineering, Empirical Software Engineering, and human aspects of software development. By connecting scientific rigor with real-world needs, SAIL seeks to generate knowledge, methods, and practical solutions that help shape the future of software and AI systems in academia and industry.

SAIL brings together researchers and students interested in advancing the engineering of software and AI-intensive systems. We study how these systems are designed, developed, evaluated, and improved, with a strong focus on quality, evidence-based research, and real-world relevance. Our goal is to build knowledge and solutions that not only move research forward, but also help address practical challenges faced by industry and society. In doing so, SAIL serves as a space for collaboration, innovation, and the training of the next generation of software and AI engineering researchers.

coordination.title: Coordination
coordination.description:
Marcos Kalinowski is the coordinator of SAIL PUC-Rio and a faculty member at the Department of Informatics at PUC-Rio. With over 15 years of experience in software engineering research, he leads initiatives in empirical software engineering, AI engineering, and human aspects of software development.

SAIL Coordination ensures that our research, partnerships, and collaborative initiatives operate smoothly while maintaining the highest standards of academic rigor and real-world impact. Under his leadership, the coordination team works to connect our research community with industry partners, foster collaboration among researchers and students, and translate our findings into practical solutions that benefit both academia and industry.
